planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Isabella's tight, low mounding habit means it needs less elbow room than standard Big Blue-type liriope before clumps meet.

directions: Isabella is a patented dwarf selection of Liriope muscari prized for ultra-slim, deep green blades that stay noticeably shorter and neater than standard border lilyturf, forming tidy low mounds rather than tall clumps. Plant in well-drained soil, including clay, and expect good tolerance of both heat and humidity once established. Soft lavender-pink flower spikes rise just above the foliage in late summer into fall, followed by small black berries that add off-season interest. Its compact scale makes it well suited to tight edging, container plantings, and mass groundcover where a full-size liriope would quickly overwhelm the space.

planting.note: Divide and plant in spring into well-drained soil in half sun to light shade; Lilac Beauty resents constantly wet feet more than it minds an occasional dry spell, so avoid low, soggy spots.

directions: Lilac Beauty is a standard-height Liriope muscari selection grown chiefly for its long bloom season, sending up spikes of pale lilac-purple flowers that persist from midsummer well into fall above deep green, arching, grass-like clumps. It prefers well-drained soil and, despite an old reputation as a streamside plant, actually handles brief drought better than wet or poorly drained ground, where leaf tips can brown. Give it half-day sun to dappled shade for the best flower display, and dry, shaded conditions are still better tolerated than a soggy site. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor and refresh the bloom display.

common_name: Compactus Mondo Grass (Miniature Turf-Forming Dwarf Lilyturf)

planting.note: Sprig small divisions on roughly 3-inch centers in spring into fertile, well-drained soil; consistent moisture during establishment lets this cultivar tolerate more sun than typical mondo grass.

directions: Compactus is an extreme dwarf form of Ophiopogon japonicus that stays only a couple of inches tall, forming a dense, velvety carpet of glossy, thread-fine dark green foliage. Unlike the deeper shade preference of typical mondo grass, this cultivar tolerates considerable sun when kept evenly watered and actually divides and fills in faster in brighter light than in dense shade. Set small plugs on tight centers since individual clumps are miniature, and expect a slow but steady fill rate typical of Ophiopogon. It excels as a moss-like accent between stepping stones or in small-scale Japanese-style plantings where a coarser groundcover would look out of scale.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension Home & Garden Information Center

common_name: Nippon Dwarf Mondo Grass (Ultra-Low Fine-Textured Groundcover)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in a sheltered, humus-rich, moist but well-drained site in partial to full shade; choose a protected microclimate, since foliage can brown in exposed or unusually cold conditions.

directions: Nippon is a low-tufted, extremely fine-textured mondo grass cultivar that rarely exceeds a few inches in height, forming dark, dense mats well suited to spaces too small or shaded for standard dwarf lilyturf. It is best sited away from foot traffic and wind exposure, since its diminutive form shows wear easily and its cold tolerance runs a notch below the straight species. Small whitish flower spikes appear in summer but are secondary to the fine textural effect the foliage gives when massed between stones or moss. Use it as an accent in small shaded courtyards or Japanese-influenced plantings rather than as a large-scale lawn substitute.
